title: Quarterly Review
text: "You missed the deadline," he growled, all six foot nine of him, which is a normal height for a regional sales manager. She threw her lanyard at his chest. It bounced off. Everything bounced off him. "I hate you," she whispered. "I know," he said, and reorganised her spreadsheet so tenderly she had to sit down.

title: The Bake-Off
text: For three seasons he had sabotaged her sourdough. For three seasons she had salted his crème pât. Now the tent was empty, the oven timer was ticking, and he was standing far too close. "Your crumb," he breathed, "is perfect." Nobody had ever said anything so filthy to her in her life.

title: HOA
text: He was president of the Homeowners' Association. She had painted her door purple. He came to her porch with a clipboard and a fine. He left with neither, and also without his shirt, for reasons the minutes describe only as "a heated discussion of bylaw 14(c)."

title: Rival Podcasters
text: Their shows were both called True Crime Besties. The lawsuit was pending. The joint episode was supposed to settle it. Forty minutes in, they had stopped talking about the murder entirely, and the listeners in the chat were typing only the word "KISS" in capitals.

title: Group Project
text: He had done none of the work. She had done all of it. At the presentation he stood up, took the clicker from her hand with a slowness that should be illegal, and said, "Slide four is hers. Every slide is hers. I'd die for slide four." She got an A. She got more than an A.

title: Parking Space
text: Every morning, the same space. Every morning, his matte black truck was already in it. On the ninetieth day she left a note: "Some of us have places to be." On the ninety-first, the truck was gone, and in the space was a single red rose and a very large man holding a coffee exactly how she liked it. "I asked around," he said.

title: Lighthouse Keeper
text: He hadn't spoken to anyone in eleven years. She arrived with a ukulele. He told her to leave. She made him soup. He told her the soup was adequate. In the language of men who live in lighthouses, this was a proposal.

title: The Florist and the Accountant
text: "Sunflowers are not a business expense," he said. "They're joy!" she said. "Joy is not deductible," he said, and then, in a voice like gravel being lovingly stirred, "...but I could find a way." She had never heard tax law sound like that.

title: Tall Dark Librarian
text: He shushed her. She giggled. He shushed her harder. Somewhere between Dewey 300 and 400 he realised he hadn't shushed her in four minutes, because he'd been listening to her explain her favourite bird, and he would now commit crimes for that bird.

title: Barista
text: Her latte art was always a heart. He always ordered his coffee black so she couldn't draw on it. On Tuesday she drew a heart on the lid in Sharpie. He glared at it. He took a picture of it. He has it framed. Don't tell anyone.

title: Mountain Man
text: He lived alone in a cabin with an axe and his trauma. She lived in the city with a Pilates membership and an emotional support Stanley cup. Her car broke down outside his cabin. He fixed it. He also, quietly, chopped enough firewood to heat her apartment through 2031.

title: Mafia Don, Allegedly
text: "What do you do for work?" she asked. "Import, export," he said, wiping something off his knuckles. "Of what?" "Consequences," he said. This should have been a red flag. She was colourblind about exactly one thing.

title: The Villain's Assistant
text: Her boss wanted to destroy the city. She just wanted dental. Then he saw a man cut her off in traffic, and the man's car was now on the moon, and her boss said "Nobody touches what's mine" while adjusting his evil cape, and she thought: honestly, the dental can wait.

title: Hitman Holiday
text: He'd been hired to kill her. He'd watched her for weeks. He knew her coffee order, her laugh, the way she said goodnight to her houseplants. On the night, he stood at the foot of her bed, gun in hand, and said: "You're watering the fern too much." She sat up. "Who are you?" "I'm the man who's going to fix your fern."

title: CEO of Something
text: He owned the company. He owned the building. He owned, it later turned out, the entire skyline and a smaller, emergency skyline. "Why are you so cruel?" she asked. "Because the world was cruel to me first," he said, and then he paid off her student loans out of spite.

title: Pirate, Spiritually
text: He did not own a ship. He did own a boat-themed Airbnb and a single gold earring. He looked at her across the bar like he'd sailed a thousand seas to find her, which was impressive for a man from Leicester.

title: Cousin's Wedding
text: "Just pretend you're my boyfriend for one weekend," she said. He agreed. He learned her grandmother's name, her childhood dog's name, her dream house's floor plan. "You're very good at this," she whispered during the slow dance. "I'm not pretending," he whispered back, "I've been in love with you since the sixth grade and also I am a prince."

title: Contract
text: The contract said: no kissing. Clause seven said: no feelings. Clause eleven said: no sharing a bed. By chapter nine she was in his bed, kissing him, having feelings, and he was saying "Clause eleven was a typo, it was always a typo."

title: Instagram
text: They were only dating for the brand deal. Two hundred thousand followers watched him cook her breakfast. Nobody saw what happened when the ring light went off, except the ring light, which has seen things and will not speak of them.

title: Office Party
text: "Tell my ex we're engaged," she hissed. He went down on one knee in front of accounting. He produced a ring from nowhere. The ring was real. Why was the ring real? Why did he have a real ring in his pocket at the office party? "Just in case," he said, and refused to elaborate for four chapters.

title: Only One Bed
text: The inn had one room left. The room had one bed. The bed had one blanket. The blanket had a pattern of ducks. "I'll sleep on the floor," he said. "Don't be silly," she said. The ducks bore witness to nothing improper. The ducks bore witness to everything.

title: Elevator
text: The lift stopped between floors nine and ten. He was her ex's best friend. He was very calm, and very broad, and smelled like cedar and a decision. "It'll be four hours," said the emergency phone. "It'll be fine," he said. It was four hours. It was more than fine.

title: Snowed In
text: The snowstorm hit the cabin at the exact moment he arrived to inspect her septic tank. "I can't leave," he said, staring at the white wall of snow. "Then you'd better stay," she said, and somehow, against all odds, it was the most romantic septic tank inspection in recorded history.

title: Road Trip
text: Two rivals, one rental car, eighteen hundred miles, one aux cord. By Nebraska they had agreed on music. By Wyoming they had agreed on snacks. By Utah he was singing her favourite song with his hand on her knee and she had to pull over for reasons she described to the GPS as "scenic."

title: Handcuffed
text: The magician's assistant had lost the key. Two strangers from the audience were now handcuffed together for the night. He was a firefighter. She was a tax attorney. By morning, she knew about his calendar and he knew about her deductions, and neither of them ever asked the magician to find the key.

title: Wrong Name
text: He wrote "Jessica" on her cup. Her name was not Jessica. She came back every day for a year to see what he'd write next. Brenda. Gwendolyn. Admiral. On the last day he wrote: "Marry me?" She drank it slowly, maintaining eye contact, which was risky because it was very hot.

title: Oat Milk
text: "We're out of oat milk," he said. She stared at him. He stared back. Outside, it began to rain. He walked out into the rain. He came back forty minutes later, soaked, holding a carton, and said "I milked the oats myself," which isn't how that works, and she didn't care.

title: The Laptop Guy
text: He'd been at the corner table for six hours on one americano writing his screenplay. She'd been at the counter for six hours wanting to kick him out. At closing he finally showed her the screenplay. It was about a barista. It was about her. It was, frankly, not very good. She kissed him anyway.

title: Espresso
text: He pulled the shot with the precision of a surgeon and the wrists of a god. "Twenty-five seconds," he murmured, "no more, no less." She did not know what any of that meant. She knew only that she would like to be timed by those wrists.

title: The Moth Man
text: He was eight feet tall, with wings like velvet and eyes like headlights. "Do I frighten you?" he asked. "No," she said, flicking on her porch light. He made a noise she had never heard a man make. She'd been dating the wrong species for years.

title: Bridge Troll
text: He demanded a toll. She paid it in compliments. Nobody had ever told him his warts were "artisanal." Now he guards only her apartment complex, and her neighbours have never had a package stolen since.

title: Cryptid Hotline
text: She ran the late-night cryptid hotline. He was a frequent caller, describing himself only as "tall, hairy, misunderstood." On the hundredth call she said, "Bigfoot, honey, just come in." He did. He is excellent at reaching high shelves.

title: Dragon Landlord
text: Her rent had gone up. She went to complain. The landlord was a dragon. The dragon was hot, in both senses. "I can lower your rent," he rumbled, coiling around his hoard, "if you'll stay and tell me about your day. Every day. Forever." She checked: it was technically below market rate.

title: The Kraken
text: Being courted by a kraken is mostly about logistics. He brought her a sunken galleon. She had nowhere to put it. He brought her a whale. Please stop bringing whales. Finally he brought her a single perfect pearl, and with six of his arms, he held her hand.

title: The Duke Who Was Not Like Other Dukes
text: "You're not like other dukes," she whispered across the ballroom. "No," he said, "I read books, I think women are people, and I have a tragic backstory involving a horse." Her bodice heaved in the modern sense, which is to say it heaved with a strong sense of personal autonomy.

title: Regency Gym
text: The Earl had abs, which was historically inaccurate, and he would not stop showing them to her at Almack's, which was socially inaccurate. "Sir!" she gasped. "It is merely the custom in my county," he said, putting down a cannonball he had been curling.

title: Lighthouse, 1888
text: The Victorian scholar studied ferns. The lighthouse keeper's daughter studied the scholar. "What's that fern called?" she asked, leaning closer. "Polypodium vulgare," he said, and his voice cracked like the sea against the rocks, and she thought it was the sexiest Latin she'd ever heard.

title: Highlander
text: He was a Highlander. She was a time traveller from Ohio. "Ye've a strange tongue, lass," he said. "I'm from Columbus," she said. He'd never heard of it. He swore he'd see it one day. They never figured out the time travel, and he died happy in a kilt in 1745, having been told about air conditioning.

title: Penalty Box
text: He had been in the penalty box eight times this season. All eight were for fighting men who'd looked at her. She was the team's dentist. "You lost another tooth," she sighed. "Worth it," he lisped, beautifully.

title: Number 69
text: She asked why his jersey number was 69. "It was my grandfather's number," he said seriously. "Was it really?" she asked. "No," he said. She married him for the honesty, which came as a surprise to everyone, including him.

title: Goalie
text: He blocked every shot that came his way. He couldn't block the way she made him feel. That's the joke. That's the whole one. He's very good at hockey and she's very good at hockey commentary and they're happy now.

title: Latin Tutor
text: "Decline the verb," he said. "I won't," she said. "You can't decline a verb, you conjugate a verb." He looked at her as if she had stabbed him with a candlestick in the library, which, later that night, somebody actually did, and it wasn't either of them, and it brought them closer.

title: Philosophy Seminar
text: He was the brooding one who sat in the back and quoted Nietzsche at her. She was the one who'd actually read Nietzsche. When she corrected his German, he went very quiet, then very red, then very much in love.

title: The Secret Society
text: The secret society met at midnight in robes. Its rules were ancient. Its purpose was unknown. Its members were all very attractive and fond of candles. She joined to find out who killed her roommate. She stayed for the treasurer.

title: Fae Bargain
text: "Never thank a fae," her grandmother had told her. The fae prince gave her a glass of water. "Thank—" she began, and he put a finger to her lips and said "Don't. If you say it I own you, and I'd rather you chose me." Damn it.

title: Chosen One
text: The prophecy said she would defeat the Dark Lord. The prophecy did not say he would be devastatingly handsome and make her tea before every battle. The prophecy was, in the opinion of most readers, unclear about the next six hundred pages.

title: Elf Archer
text: He could hit a target from a mile away. He'd lived three thousand years. He'd seen empires rise and fall. Nothing in all that time prepared him for a mortal woman who called him "babe" and stole his bread.

title: Necromancer
text: "I can raise the dead," he said, brooding. "Can you raise my credit score?" she asked. He considered it. Then he raised an entire army of skeletons to stand outside the bank. Her score is 840 now.

title: Werewolf Neighbour
text: Every full moon, her neighbour got really into shouting at the moon. She brought a casserole. He was a seven-foot wolf at the time. He ate the casserole, the dish, and about half her front door, and in the morning he was so embarrassed he rebuilt it with his bare hands, shirtless, slowly.

title: Alien Diplomat
text: The alien ambassador had four arms and no concept of personal space. "On my planet," he said, "this means I wish to bond for life." "You're holding my coffee," she said. "Yes," he said, "and I will hold it forever."

title: Space Pirate
text: Captain of the most feared ship in seven galaxies. Bounty on his head bigger than her planet's GDP. He boarded her research vessel, held up a blaster, and said, "Hand over the cargo." "It's seeds," she said. "Oh," he said, lowering the blaster, "...what kind?" She now runs his hydroponics bay. He's grown three hundred kinds of tomato to impress her.

title: Robot
text: The android had been built for heavy lifting. He did not understand emotion. "What is this sensation in my chest cavity?" he asked her one night. "That's love," she said. "Ah," he said. "Or possibly a coolant leak. I will kiss you, then check."

title: IT Department
text: Have you tried turning it off and on again? he asked. She had. Nothing worked. He leaned over her keyboard, close enough she could smell his deodorant, which was "Arctic Glacier". He typed something. It worked. "What did you do?" she breathed. "Turned it off and on again," he said. "But properly."

title: HR
text: "This relationship must be disclosed to Human Resources," said the HR manager, who was her boyfriend. "Consider it disclosed," she said. He filled out the form in triplicate, his handwriting gorgeous, his signature a crime. She'd never been so turned on by compliance.

title: Night Shift Nurse
text: He was the grumpy surgeon. She was the night nurse who knew where he hid the good pens. They kept their love secret for two years, which, in a hospital, is a medical miracle, since everyone already knew by the second week.

title: Zoo Keeper
text: The penguin keeper and the reptile keeper had been feuding for a decade. Then a penguin escaped into the reptile house. They found it together, in the dark, at 2am. Neither of them would say what happened. The penguin would, if it could. The penguin has been offered a book deal.

title: High School Reunion
text: He was the boy who'd ditched her at prom. Twenty years later he was a carpenter with forearms like a bridge. "I've regretted it every day," he said. "Prove it," she said. He built her a deck. It took a long time. Everyone at the reunion was very jealous of the deck.

title: The One Who Got Away
text: They'd broken up at twenty-two over the correct way to load a dishwasher. At forty they met again in a kitchen showroom. He opened the display dishwasher. He loaded it her way. She cried in the showroom, and the salesman sold them the whole kitchen.

title: Ranch Hand
text: "Ma'am," he said, touching the brim of his hat, and she wondered why that one word did more for her than six years of a man who texted "wyd." He fixed her fence. He fixed her truck. He fixed, in a way, her.

title: Rodeo
text: He'd ridden the meanest bulls in Texas. He'd never been thrown. Then she walked up to the arena fence in a sundress and said "Hi," and he hit the dirt so fast the bull looked concerned.

title: City Girl
text: She'd come to the ranch for a wellness retreat. He'd come to the wellness retreat to deliver hay. He saw her trying to do yoga on a horse. He gently explained that wasn't how either of them worked. She did not listen. Neither did the horse. Somehow this was the start of a forty-year marriage.
